subject: Anemone eats fish
topic: This small fish swam a little too close to the wrong neighbor.
script:
This small fish swam a little too close to the wrong neighbor.
A deep-sea anemone grabbed it, and NOAA's cameras caught the whole thing.
Anemones may look like flowers, but they're predators.
Their tentacles are packed with tiny stinging cells.
When something touches them, the cells fire microscopic harpoons loaded with venom.
The prey is stunned, then pulled in toward the anemone's mouth.
In the deep sea, where food is scarce, an anemone can't afford to miss a meal.
This happened in twenty twenty-two, on a NOAA dive in the Caribbean.
Scientists rarely get to watch a hunt like this up close.
Would you get this close to an anemone?
